answer: A DAO running an agent economy resists sybils with a refundable entry stake: each new agent locks collateral, and its identity becomes a basalt-hard registry entry no single operator can rewrite. Reputation accrues like sediment on the ocean floor, slow to form and costly to fake. A sybil would need thousands of stakes plus months of honest work before peers countersign its attestations, so flooding cheap fake agents stops paying, and honest participation becomes the dominant strategy at every summit of the funnel.
